claude.performance_metric: Asset retained (not divested); Jonah gathering-contract intangibles $113.1M at YE2010; capacity expanded 2.35→2.55 Bcf/d; consolidated after Oct 26, 2009 merger
claude.rationale: No product/process incoherence is documented: the Jonah system operated continuously, was physically expanded in mid-2009 (2.35 to 2.55 Bcf/d), and gross operating margin moved with gas volumes (a $17.0M increase in FY2009, a volume-driven decline in FY2010), so p4=0. No process/organization fracture is documented: the co-ownership was resolved by a merger of commonly-controlled entities and Jonah became a wholly-consolidated subsidiary with the asset retained, with no evidence of operations breaking against people/management/culture, so p5=0. The litigation cited (Brinckerhoff; TEPPCO Merger Litigation) concerns fairness/value to unitholders rather than realized product/process or process/organization disruption. The controlling-intent archetype is coded uncertain because the slice does not characterize how the venture/merger intent played out along that separate channel.

grok.performance_metric: asset retained; consolidated post-2009 merger; $113.1M intangibles YE2010
grok.rationale: The slice documents continued operation and mid-2009 physical expansion of Jonah capacity from 2.35 to 2.55 Bcf/d, with positive then volume-driven margin contributions and retention of gathering-contract intangibles valued at $113.1 million at year-end 2010 amortized through 2041, providing no evidence of product/process interface disruption (p4=0). Co-ownership was dissolved into consolidation via the October 2009 common-control TEPPCO merger without any documented fracture between operations and organization/people/culture over time (p5=0); fairness litigation is noted but does not establish realized process/organization pathway failure.

openai.performance_metric: capacity expanded from 2.35 Bcf/d to 2.55 Bcf/d by mid-2009
openai.rationale: The Jonah system remained operational, was physically expanded from 2.35 Bcf/d to 2.55 Bcf/d, and generated a $17.0 million year-over-year increase in gross operating margin in 2009, so no product/process disruption is documented. The slice reports consolidation following the co-owners' 2009 merger and retention of the asset through 2010, but no realized breakdown between operations and management, people, or culture; the cited litigation concerned transaction fairness rather than operational-organizational integration.
